I farm 7 mu in a wheat-maize rotation, so I will use the same 7 mu for winter wheat first and then summer maize after wheat harvest. I have farmed for 35 years, and with a small farm and some family labor working off-farm, I will keep the plan steady and practical instead of trying anything complicated. Because I have well irrigation, I will rely on a few key irrigations to protect yield. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put on enough nitrogen to support tillering and grain filling, add phosphorus for roots, and a moderate amount of potassium. I will use rotary tillage because it is fast and suits my scale. I will spray a couple of times to control weeds and diseases if needed. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because that is what I would trust for yield in my area. I will keep fertilizer at a moderate level, give a few irrigations at important stages, and use fewer pesticide sprays than wheat unless pests become serious. I will continue rotary tillage because it saves labor and fits my machinery and habits.
